name: Crossing the Delaware
summary: At dusk the army begins to cross the Delaware at McKonkey's Ferry in Durham boats and ferries, in sleet and floating ice; the crossing runs about three hours late.

name: Alarm at Trenton
summary: A party fires on the Pennington road picket on Christmas evening; the garrison turns out and the post is reinforced.

name: Crossing complete
summary: The last troops and guns reach the New Jersey bank, about three hours late. Knox had the infantry over by about 02:00; the Army's campaign history has 03:00, with the guns an hour later.

name: March begins
summary: The column sets off for Trenton, about nine miles away.
playback_text: The column sets off from the landing for Trenton, about nine miles away.

name: Army divides
summary: At Birmingham Greene takes the upper road and Sullivan the River Road.

name: First shots
summary: Greene's advance drives in Lt. Wiederhold's picket on the Pennington Road.
playback_text: Greene's advance drives in Lt. Wiederhold's picket on the Pennington road.

name: Sullivan's attack
summary: About three minutes later the lower column strikes the jäger picket at the Hermitage.

name: Guns open
summary: Forrest's and Hamilton's batteries open from the head of King and Queen Streets.

name: Hessian guns taken
summary: The Rall regiment's two guns are lost on King Street, just north of the headquarters.

name: Line of battle
summary: The three regiments form a line along the east edge of the village.
playback_text: The three Hessian regiments form a line along the east edge of the village.

name: Rall shot
summary: Rall leads the Rall and Lossberg regiments back into the town and is mortally wounded on Queen Street.
playback_text: Rall leads two regiments back into the town and is mortally wounded on Queen Street.

name: Surrender in the orchard
summary: Lt. Col. Scheffer surrenders the Rall and von Lossberg regiments in the orchard east of the town.

name: Knyphausen surrenders
summary: The Knyphausen regiment, cut off from the bridge, surrenders by the Assunpink a quarter mile away, shortly after the others. About fifty men get over the creek.

name: Return to Pennsylvania
summary: The army starts back across the Delaware with its prisoners.

name: Escape over the bridge
summary: The jägers and the twenty British dragoons get away over the Assunpink bridge before Sullivan's men reach it.

name: The escapers get away
summary: The British dragoons reach Princeton, the jägers Bordentown, and about fifty men of the Knyphausen regiment, who forded the Assunpink, make for Crosswicks. Some 400 to 600 of the garrison got away in all.

name: Morgan forms for battle
summary: About an hour before daylight a scout reports Tarleton within five miles. Morgan turns his men out and puts them in three lines across the Green River Road: riflemen in front, Pickens's militia behind them, and Howard's Continentals and Virginians on the rise behind, with Washington's cavalry in reserve.

name: The pickets are driven in
summary: About day, Tarleton's advance guard of Legion dragoons drives in Capt. Inman's mounted pickets on the Green River Road and finds the Americans drawn up to fight.

name: Tarleton deploys
summary: The British come out of the woods and form one line in sight of the Americans: light infantry on the right, the Legion infantry in the centre, the 7th Fusiliers on the left, a 3-pounder in each gap and fifty dragoons on each flank. The 71st Highlanders and about 200 Legion cavalry stand in reserve 150 yards back.

name: First shots
summary: Tarleton sends Ogilvie's Legion dragoons to drive in the riflemen in front. The riflemen fire from behind the trees and the dragoons come back with empty saddles. Militia veterans gave John Savage of Brandon's regiment the first shot.

name: The British line advances
summary: About sunrise the two guns open and the whole line comes on with three cheers. Morgan answers along the militia line: "They gave us the British halloo, boys, give them the Indian halloo."

name: The skirmishers fall back
summary: McDowell's and Cunningham's riflemen, having picked off officers at long range, fall back on Pickens's line.

name: The militia volleys
summary: Pickens's militia hold their fire until the British are within killing distance, then fire by regiments: "pop, pop, pop, and then a whole volley". The British line halts to dress and comes on again.

name: The militia withdraw; dragoons ride them down
summary: As ordered, the militia file off round Howard's line, most of them round its left, to re-form in rear. The 17th Light Dragoons on Tarleton's right charge after them towards their horses; Washington's cavalry strikes the dragoons and drives them back.

name: Line against line
summary: The British infantry close on Howard's line and the two fire at close range, neither giving way. Tarleton orders up the 71st on his left to turn Howard's right, and the reserve cavalry to follow it; the cavalry does not come.

name: Howard's line falls back
summary: Howard orders his right company to face the Highlanders. The order goes wrong; the company faces about, and the rest of the line, taking it for a retreat, marches to the rear in good order. Morgan picks the ground for it to halt, about 80 to 100 yards back.

name: Face about: volley and bayonet
summary: The British, sure the day is won, rush on out of order. At 10 to 30 yards Howard's line faces about and fires; then it charges with the bayonet. The British line stops, breaks and runs.

name: Double envelopment
summary: Washington's cavalry rides round the British right and into their rear; Pickens's militia come back into the fight round the American right, onto the 71st. The infantry throw down their arms. The gunners fight to the last by their two 3-pounders, which are taken.

name: Tarleton's last charge
summary: The Legion cavalry will not charge and about 200 of them leave the field. Tarleton leads some fifty horsemen, most of them of the 17th Light Dragoons, at the American cavalry and is beaten off; he and Washington cross swords before he rides away down the Green River Road.

name: Pursuit
summary: Washington and Pickens follow Tarleton for 22 to 24 miles without catching him; the British burn most of their baggage. Morgan counts over 500 prisoners, two guns and two colours for 12 killed and about 60 wounded, and marches off the field the same day to get the prisoners away from Cornwallis.

name: Charleston: arms and powder seized
summary: Patriot leaders carry off the arms stored in the State House attic and powder from two outlying magazines, without a fight. [T01]

name: Fort Charlotte surrenders
summary: Major James Mayson takes the royal fort on the Savannah River in the Council of Safety's name; the garrison gives it up. [T02]

name: Fort Johnson taken
summary: South Carolina troops under Colonel Isaac Motte walk into Fort Johnson, whose guns the royal navy had just disabled. [T03]

name: Ninety Six: Savage's Old Field
summary: Loyalists surround Major Williamson's Patriot stockade near Ninety Six. Neither side wins; a truce ends the first bloodshed in the state. [T04]

name: Great Cane Brake
summary: Colonel Thomson's rangers and militia surprise a Loyalist camp on the Reedy River and take over a hundred prisoners. [T05]

name: Snow Campaign
summary: Richardson's militia, thousands strong, march through the backcountry; the Loyalist leaders are seized or scattered and snow ends the campaign. [T06]

name: Sullivan's Island (Fort Sullivan)
summary: The unfinished palmetto fort at the harbour mouth drives off the British fleet. [T07]

name: Breach Inlet
summary: Clinton's troops on Long Island find the inlet too deep to wade and cannot cross to Sullivan's Island. [T08]

name: Cherokee War begins
summary: The Cherokee strike the western settlements; the war runs to the treaty of 20 May 1777. [T09]

name: Esseneca (Seneca Old Town)
summary: The Cherokee, with Loyalists under Cameron, ambush Williamson's column at Esseneca before dawn; his men break, Hammond's charge drives the attackers off, and the town is burned. [T10]

name: Tamassee and the Ring Fight
summary: Williamson's men beat a large Cherokee war party (Pickens's Ring Fight near Tamassee) and burn the Lower Towns. [T11]

name: Capture of privateers, Charleston
summary: The only action the Archives list gives for 1778. Neither the list nor any source read says who took which ships. [T12]

name: Port Royal Island (Beaufort)
summary: Moultrie's Continentals and militia beat a British detachment under Major Gardiner near Gray's Hill. [T13]

name: Prevost before Charleston
summary: Prevost's army reaches the Charleston lines, then breaks off and withdraws when it learns Lincoln is hurrying back. [T14]

name: Stono Ferry
summary: Lincoln attacks the British rear guard at the ferry and is repulsed; both sides lose heavily. [T15]

name: Siege of Charleston
summary: Clinton's army and fleet besiege the city; on 12 May Lincoln surrenders the army. [T16]

name: Monck's Corner
summary: Tarleton's dragoons surprise Huger's cavalry and militia before dawn, taking horses and wagons and cutting Charleston off. [T17]

name: Lenud's Ferry
summary: Tarleton surprises the American cavalry at the Santee crossing and scatters it. [T18]

name: Waxhaws (Buford's defeat)
summary: Tarleton's Legion overtakes Buford's Virginians and cuts them down as they try to surrender. [T19]

name: Alexander's Old Field (Beckhamville)
summary: Captain John McClure's Whigs rout a Loyalist muster at Alexander's Old Field (Beckhamville). [T20]

name: Huck's Defeat (Williamson's Plantation)
summary: Patriot militia surprise Captain Huck's Loyalist and British detachment; Huck is killed. [T21]

name: Rocky Mount
summary: Sumter attacks Turnbull's post three times and cannot take it; he withdraws. [T22]

name: Hanging Rock I (Davie's raid)
summary: Davie's North Carolinians ambush a Loyalist party near Hanging Rock and take horses and arms. [T23]

name: Hanging Rock II
summary: Sumter attacks the Loyalist camp at Hanging Rock; heavy losses on both sides, and the Americans leave without holding the post. [T24]

name: Camden
summary: Cornwallis routs Gates's army north of Camden and takes its guns and wagons. [T25]

name: Cary's Fort (Sumter's raid)
summary: Sumter's men under Colonel Taylor take Cary's redoubt at Wateree Ferry and a convoy on its way from Ninety Six. [T26]

name: Fishing Creek
summary: Tarleton surprises Sumter's camp, scatters his command and retakes the convoy and prisoners. [T27]

name: Musgrove Mill
summary: Patriot militia ambush and beat a Loyalist and British force at the Enoree. [T28]

name: Nelson's Ferry
summary: Marion surprises the guard at Sumter's Great Savannah plantation near Nelson's Ferry and frees about 150 Maryland Continentals taken at Camden. [T29]

name: Blue Savannah
summary: Marion ambushes Loyalists at Blue Savannah. Read in Morgan's list, the NPS timeline and the Archives list only. [T30]

name: Black Mingo
summary: Marion attacks a Loyalist camp near midnight and drives it into the swamp. [T31]

name: Kings Mountain
summary: Frontier militia surround and destroy Ferguson's Loyalist force on the ridge. [T32]

name: Tearcoat Swamp
summary: Marion's midnight attack routs Tynes's Loyalist camp. [T33]

name: Fish Dam Ford
summary: Wemyss's night attack on Sumter's camp fails; Wemyss is wounded and taken. [T34]

name: Blackstock's
summary: Tarleton attacks Sumter's position and is beaten back with heavy loss; Sumter is badly wounded. [T35]

name: Rugeley's Mill
summary: Washington's dragoons bluff Colonel Rugeley's Loyalists out of their fortified barn at Clermont with a log painted as a cannon; they surrender without a shot. [T36]

name: Halfway Swamp
summary: Marion meets Major McLeroth's detachment of the 64th Foot; McLeroth answers with a challenge to a fight of twenty picked men, then slips away, and a shot is fired at Singleton's Mill the next day. [T37]

name: Hammond's Store
summary: Washington's dragoons ride down a Loyalist force sent from Georgia. [T38]

name: Cowpens
summary: Morgan defeats Tarleton's British regulars. [T39]

name: Georgetown raid
summary: Marion and Lee surprise the garrison and take its commander, but without guns they cannot break into the post, and withdraw. [T40]

name: Beattie's Mill
summary: American victory (ABT only, in Morgan's list). Not on the NPS timeline; no other source read. [T41]

name: Fort Watson surrenders
summary: Lee's Legion and Marion besiege the post until the British surrender. [T42]

name: Hobkirk's Hill
summary: Greene is beaten by Rawdon, who holds the field; Greene retreats. [T43]

name: Fort Motte
summary: The garrison is forced out when the post is set on fire. [T44]

name: Camden evacuated
summary: Rawdon abandons Camden. [T45]

name: Orangeburg, Fort Granby, Fort Galphin
summary: Three posts fall to Sumter and Lee (11, 15 and 19 May on the NPS timeline). [T46]

name: Siege of Ninety Six
summary: Greene's assault of 18 June is repelled; the siege is lifted as British reinforcements approach. [T47]

name: Biggin Church and Quinby Bridge
summary: The British attack at Biggin Church is broken; at Quinby Bridge the Americans cannot force a retreat. [T48]

name: Parker's Ferry
summary: American victory (ABT only, in Morgan's list). Not on the NPS timeline; no other source read. [T49]

name: Eutaw Springs
summary: Greene attacks the British camp; the British hold the field and then withdraw. A costly fight; scored differently by different sources. [T50]

name: Cornwallis marches on Guilford
summary: Cornwallis leaves his camp near Deep River Friends Meeting House at daybreak, sending his baggage away under guard. Tarleton leads with the Legion cavalry, the Guards light infantry and the jägers. Greene's army is at Guilford Courthouse, twelve miles off; Lee's Legion and Campbell's riflemen are out on the road.

name: Lee charges in the lane
summary: Lee's cavalry, falling back before Tarleton's, turns in a fenced lane and rides down his leading section. Tarleton sounds the retreat and leaves the road. The hour is disputed.

name: The Guards fire at New Garden Meeting House
summary: Lee, following by the meeting house to cut Tarleton off, rides into the Guards light infantry, who fire a volley; his horse throws him. The Legion infantry and Campbell's riflemen come up and the fight becomes general.

name: The 23rd comes up; Lee draws off
summary: The head of the British column, the 23rd Foot, arrives. Lee falls back to the cross road, covers his infantry with the cavalry and retires up the great road to the army, unpursued. Each side has lost perhaps 40 men.

name: Greene forms three lines
summary: Greene posts the North Carolina militia behind a rail fence at the edge of the woods, the Virginia militia in the woods 300 yards behind, and the Continentals on the high ground west of the courthouse, with riflemen and cavalry on each flank of the first line and two guns in the road.

name: Cannonade; the British deploy
summary: As the British column crosses Little Horsepen Creek, Singleton's 6-pounders open on it from the road. Macleod's guns answer for about half an hour while Cornwallis forms line: Webster's brigade left of the road, Leslie's right, the Guards in support, the cavalry in the road.

name: The first line breaks
summary: The British cross the muddy fields. The North Carolinians fire at 140 yards, some a second time; the British fire once at close range and charge. Most of the militia run. On both flanks the riflemen and light troops hold and fire into the ends of the British line.

name: The flanks pull the British line apart
summary: Webster turns the 33rd, the jägers and the Guards light infantry against Lynch, Kirkwood and Washington; Leslie turns von Bose and the 1st Guards against Campbell and Lee. The 2nd Guards and the grenadiers come into the line by the road. Every British foot soldier is now engaged.

name: The second line: the Virginians hold, then break
summary: In thick woods the Virginia militia fight for the better part of an hour. Lawson's brigade north of the road gives way first; Stevens's holds against the 71st until he is shot through the thigh and orders it off.

name: The separate fight in the south
summary: Von Bose and the 1st Guards follow Campbell's riflemen and Lee's infantry south-east through the woods, a mile from the road. The Guards battalion is broken on a wooded height and rallies behind the Hessians. Neither commander knows how this fight is going.

name: Webster attacks the third line and is thrown back
summary: Webster, first out of the woods, crosses the vale with the 33rd and the light troops against the Continental right. The 1st Maryland, Hawes's Virginians and Kirkwood meet him with a close volley and drive him back across the vale. He is mortally wounded.

name: The 2nd Guards break the 2nd Maryland
summary: The 2nd Battalion of Guards charges the left of the Continental line. The 2nd Maryland, new levies, gives way almost without firing, and the Guards take Singleton's two guns and press on behind the line. Greene, seeing his left turned, orders the retreat.

name: Washington and the 1st Maryland strike the Guards
summary: Washington's dragoons ride through the Guards from behind while the 1st Maryland, facing about, fires into their flank and closes with the bayonet. Lt. Col. Stuart is killed, the guns are retaken, and the Guards are driven back into the open field.

name: Cornwallis's guns stop the pursuit
summary: From the rise where the road leaves the woods Cornwallis has two 3-pounders fire grapeshot into the melee. It checks the Americans. The 23rd and 71st come out of the woods, and O'Hara, though wounded, rallies the Guards on the grenadiers. Whether he fired knowingly into his own Guards, over O'Hara's protest, is disputed (GH08).

name: Greene retreats by the Reedy Fork road
summary: The Continentals go off in good order, Green's regiment and Washington covering. Hawes's regiment, the last engaged, checks the 33rd. The four guns are left, their horses killed. The British follow a short way and stop: Greene halts three miles off at the Reedy Fork, then marches to the iron works on Troublesome Creek.

name: Tarleton's last charge
summary: Hearing fire still on the right, Cornwallis sends Tarleton there with a squadron. Lee has already drawn his Legion off towards the courthouse. Tarleton charges the riflemen who remain and scatters them: the last fight of the day.
